Team — reviewed Acme's redlines. High-level legal view and recommended compromise below (keeping in mind product risk and our position to customers):

1) Assignment of output: not acceptable. Assignment transfers IP and prevents us from reusing common components; also creates downstream risk for multi-tenant models. Counter-proposal: exclusive or non-exclusive "Customer Output License". We should offer a non-exclusive, perpetual, worldwide license to use, reproduce, modify, and distribute output for Customer's internal business purposes and for their products, subject to limitations (no ownership transfer). Sample clause: "Customer is granted a non-exclusive, perpetual, worldwide license to use Generated Output for its internal business and productization of Customer-owned offerings; Redwood retains all model-level rights and underlying technology."

2) Training/retraining: cannot grant blanket right to retrain our hosted models (that would expose our models and IP). Offer two alternatives: (A) Data used for service improvement — allow use under a narrowly scoped feedback/data license with strong anonymization and telemetry controls; (B) Paid retrain/transfer option — if Customer wants model-level retraining rights, do a separate commercial engagement (SOW) with a fee and data transfer terms. Recommended clause phrasing and redline in attached: redline_proposed_excerpt.docx

3) Feedback license: accept a limited, royalty-free license for feedback submitted via formal channels, limited to improving the Service and not for model assignment or resale. Exclude any Customer-provided copyrighted training corpus that Customer clearly marks as Confidential and not to be used.

4) Proof/onboarding evidence: ask Product for a short runbook on how we would quarantine sensitive Acme datasets and the opt-in process for paid retrain; this helps procurement accept the SOW path. Ben: can you price/estimate a retrain engagement?

I'll prepare a tracked-changes counter and propose the above language. If we present this as a balanced set (license + paid retrain path + concessions), we should be able to close without assignment.

Jordan / Katie — thanks for the redline and for your patience while we reviewed. Attached is our tracked-changes counter and a short commercial appendix (redline_proposed_excerpt.docx, Draft_Order_Form_v3.xlsx). Summary of the compromise we can sign up to: 

1) Output: Redwood will not assign generated output. Instead we will provide Customer a non-exclusive, perpetual, worldwide license to use Generated Output for Customer's internal business and to productize within Customer-owned products. This preserves our model-level IP while meeting ACME's productization needs.

2) Training/retraining: Redwood will not allow Acme to unilaterally retrain our hosted models. Two options are available: (A) Data contributed via normal service interactions can be used to improve the Service under a limited feedback/data license with safeguards (anonymization, telemetry, opt-out/segregation for flagged datasets); (B) If Acme requires model retraining or model export, we will execute a paid SOW with explicit data handling, scope, and compensation. Ben has outlined a ballpark for the SOW — happy to include a commercial appendix.

3) Feedback license: Redwood will accept a royalty-free license to use Customer feedback for Service improvement, limited in scope and with exclusions for materials Customer clearly marks as confidential or proprietary for which they reserve use-rights.
